81: /// Scans a [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/) inline script
82: /// block using the source locator and the opening tag range.
83: struct ScriptTagScanner<'a> {
84:     locator: &'a Locator<'a>,
85:     script_start: TextRange,
86: }

88: impl<'a> ScriptTagScanner<'a> {
89:     /// Parses the rest of a [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/)
90:     /// script comment and moves `comments` past the script comment's end unless
91:     /// the script comment is invalid.
92:     ///
93:     /// Returns `true` if it is a valid script comment.
94:     fn skip_script_comments<I>(&self, comments: &mut std::iter::Peekable<I>) -> bool
95:     where
96:         I: Iterator<Item = TextRange>,
97:     {
98:         let contents = self.locator.contents();
99:         let index = self.locator.to_index();
100:         let source = SourceCode::new(contents, index);
101:         let start_location = source.source_location(self.script_start.start());
102:         let tag_offset = index.offset(start_location.row, start_location.column, contents);
103:         let line_end = self
104:             .locator
105:             .full_line_end(tag_offset.max(self.script_start.end()));
106:         let rest = self.locator.after(line_end);
107:         let mut end_offset = None;
108:         let mut lines = UniversalNewlineIterator::with_offset(rest, line_end);
109: 
110:         while let Some(line) = lines.next() {
111:             let line_text = line.as_str();
112:             let Some(content) = script_line_content(line_text) else {
113:                 break;
114:             };
115: 
116:             if content == "///" {
117:                 // > Precedence for an ending line # /// is given when the next line is not a valid
118:                 // > embedded content line as described above.
119:                 // > For example, the following is a single fully valid block:
120:                 // > ```python
121:                 // > # /// some-toml
122:                 // > # embedded-csharp = """
123:                 // > # /// <summary>
124:                 // > # /// text
125:                 // > # ///
126:                 // > # /// </summary>
127:                 // > # public class MyClass { }
128:                 // > # """
129:                 // > # ///
130:                 // ````
131:                 if lines
132:                     .next()
133:                     .is_some_and(|next_line| is_valid_script_line(next_line.as_str()))
134:                 {
135:                     continue;
136:                 }
137:                 end_offset = Some(line.start() + line.as_full_str().text_len());
138:                 break;
139:             }
140:         }
141: 
142:         // > Unclosed blocks MUST be ignored.
143:         let Some(end_offset) = end_offset else {
144:             return false;
145:         };
146: 
147:         // Skip over all script-comments.
148:         while let Some(comment) = comments.peek() {
149:             if comment.start() >= end_offset {
150:                 break;
151:             }
152: 
153:             comments.next();
154:         }
155: 
156:         true
157:     }
158: }

160: fn script_line_content(line: &str) -> Option<&str> {
161:     let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix('#') else {
162:         // Not a comment
163:         return None;
164:     };
165: 
166:     // An empty line
167:     if rest.is_empty() {
168:         return Some("");
169:     }
170: 
171:     // > If there are characters after the # then the first character MUST be a space.
172:     rest.strip_prefix(' ')

**Root cause:** In `ScriptTagScanner::skip_script_comments` (crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/eradicate/rules/commented_out_code.rs), when a bare `# ///` line was followed by a valid embedded-content line (per PEP 723 precedence, e.g. the trailing `#` comment), the scanner continued searching for another closing tag. If the scan ends without a definitive closing tag, the last such fallback is treated as the block end (so trailing comments after the metadata block are checked normally), while a block with no `# ///` at all remains flagged as before.
